chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from some of his companions, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
The saddle is a detestable riding position for women.

key_terms.السَّرْج: saddle — specifically the straddle-style riding saddle used by men; women were expected to ride in a different posture (sideways, on a litter, or on a pannier)
key_terms.مَلْعُون: detestable/cursed — in jurisprudential usage, this term indicates strong dislike (karahah shadidah) rather than outright prohibition (haram)

ai.seo_question: Is it forbidden or detestable for women to ride a saddle in Shia Islam?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (AS) states that riding in a saddle (in the manner of men, straddling a horse) is detestable for women. This hadith is found in the chapter on animal equipment (al-Kafi, Book 6) and reflects early Islamic guidance on proper conduct for women in public travel. The term 'mal'un' (detestable/cursed) in classical jurisprudential language often indicates strong prohibition or moral disapproval rather than literal cursing.

en.hubeali:
Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from one of his companions, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:
‘The saddle riding is detestable for the women’.
en.sarwar: 1. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from ibn abu ‘Umayr from certain persons of his people who has said the following: “Abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said, ‘
The saddle is a condemned riding thing for women.”’
